summary.text: A magnetosphere is the region of space around a planet or other body where charged particles are affected by that body's magnetic field.
It is created by an active dynamo inside the body, and planets with one, like Earth, can soften or block solar and cosmic radiation.
At the magnetopause the planet's field pressure balances the solar wind's, and on the opposite side the magnetosphere stretches far out into a magnetotail.

facts.label: Radiation belt found
facts.value: Van Allen belt, observed by Explorer 1 in 1958

facts.label: Planets with their own
facts.value: Mercury, Earth, Jupiter, Saturn, Uranus, Neptune

facts.label: Venus
facts.value: Only an induced field, with no inner dynamo

items.prompt: A planet has no working dynamo inside it, but the solar wind still flows past. What sort of magnetic bubble can it have?

options.label: One as strong as Earth's, from its own field
An induced one from the solar wind wrapping around it
None, because the solar wind cannot reach it
A long tail with nothing on the sunward side

items.explain: Without its own field opposing the solar wind, a body gets an induced magnetosphere, formed as the solar wind wraps around it, as at Venus.

items.prompt: Two pushes meet at the magnetopause, one from the Sun's wind and one from the planet. What is true about them there?

options.label: The planet's field pressure balances the solar wind's
The solar wind always wins and reaches the ground
The planet's field pushes the solar wind back to the Sun
Neither push exists at that boundary

items.explain: The magnetopause is defined as the place where the pressure of the planet's field is balanced by the pressure of the solar wind.

items.prompt: A burst of solar wind suddenly pushes much harder on Earth. What happens to the magnetopause?

options.label: It stays fixed in exactly the same place
It disappears completely for a while
It changes its size and shape
It jumps to Earth's night side

items.explain: Because the boundary sits where the pressures balance, it changes size and shape as the solar wind's pressure rises and falls.

items.prompt: In 1958 the first Explorer satellite was sent up to measure cosmic rays above the atmosphere. What did it find?

options.label: That Earth has no magnetic field in space
A second moon orbiting inside the field
That cosmic rays never reach near Earth
A belt of radiation trapped around Earth

items.explain: Explorer 1 observed the Van Allen radiation belt in the inner magnetosphere, and Explorer 3 confirmed it later that year.

items.prompt: Which of these planets has no field of its own, so its only magnetic field comes from the solar wind wrapping around it?

options.label: Jupiter
Saturn
Venus
Neptune

items.explain: Venus appears to have no internal dynamo, while Jupiter, Saturn and Neptune all have intrinsic magnetospheres.

items.prompt: Close to Earth the field lines look like a simple bar magnet's. Why do they look very different far out in space?

options.label: The Moon's gravity bends them out of shape
They fade away just above the atmosphere
Earth's spin ties them into knots
Flowing plasma from the Sun distorts them

items.explain: Farther out, field lines are strongly distorted by the flow of electrically conducting plasma from the Sun, the solar wind.
